faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate for education support?

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Education Support Salary: Hourly to Annual

If you work in education support—whether as a teacher’s aide, administrative officer, or student services coordinator—you may be paid an hourly rate or offered a salary. Understanding how your **education support salary** translates from hourly to annual is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, and planning your tax and super. This guide walks you through the conversion, explains the National Minimum Wage versus award rates, and shows how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula

The standard conversion is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time education support roles, the typical week is 38 hours. If you are part-time or casual, use your actual weekly hours.

For example, if your education support hourly rate is $30.00 and you work 38 hours:

$30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year (gross)

If you receive a salary offer, you can reverse the calculation to find your implied hourly rate: divide the annual salary by 52 then by your weekly hours.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, many education support roles are covered by awards—such as the Educational Services (Schools) General Staff Award or the Children’s Services Award—which set higher minimum rates. These award rates vary by classification and experience. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award.

It is important to check your specific award or enterprise agreement rather than relying solely on the National Minimum Wage. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site explains the current rates.

### Industry Averages vs Job Medians

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings. For the Education and Training industry, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,197.90 per week in May 2026. This is an industry average, not a median for any specific job such as education support. Your actual **education support salary** may be higher or lower depending on your role, location, and experience. Use the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) reference tables for broader context.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many education support employees are paid fortnightly. To estimate your gross fortnightly pay:

**Fortnightly gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 2**

Using the same $30.00 per hour, 38-hour week example:

$30.00 × 38 × 2 = $2,280 per fortnight (gross)

This can help you match your budget to your pay cycle.

### Casual Loading

If you work casually, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% casual loading. Do not add the loading on top of a rate that already includes it. On [the timesheet](/) page, you can enter your base hourly rate and tick a checkbox to add 25% casual loading. The calculator then shows the loaded rate and the resulting annual and fortnightly figures.

### Tax on Your Education Support Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. The 2026–27 Medicare levy reduction thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide, so the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used for estimates. This is an estimate only; your actual tax depends on your total income, deductions, and offsets.

### Superannuation

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. If your annual gross exceeds that, super is capped. For example, on a $59,280 annual **education support salary**, super would be $7,113.60 (12% of $59,280) added by your employer. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Putting It All Together

Let’s calculate take-home pay for a full-time education support employee earning $30.00 per hour, 38 hours per week:

- Annual gross: $59,280
- Fortnightly gross: $2,280
- Estimated tax (using 2026–27 rates, no HELP or surcharge): approximately $9,088
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,185.60
- Net annual: $59,280 – $9,088 – $1,185.60 = $49,006.40
- Net fortnightly: about $1,884.86
- Super paid on top: $7,113.60 per year

Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page to run your own numbers.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Final Thoughts

Knowing how your **education support salary** converts from hourly to annual helps you compare job offers, plan your budget, and understand your tax and super obligations. Always refer to your award or enterprise agreement for your correct minimum rate, and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman if you are unsure. For a quick calculation, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your details.
